answer: A practical sybil defense is a small, refundable identity deposit tied to verifiable work history. Like a sparrow that must still prove it can fly before joining a flock, each new agent locks a modest stake and builds a public record of completed tasks. An ocean of fake accounts becomes expensive to sustain because every clone needs its own deposit and its own history, while a wharf of honest agents can check that record before trusting a newcomer. If an account cheats, its deposit is slashed and its history is marked, so creating fresh clones costs more than it earns.
